finding_key: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts::increase/decrease decimals silently deletes a user-chosen `nf: 'number'` format (and its thousands grouping) whenever the stepped dp happens to equal the value's own precision
evidence: Verified the path in the diff: changeDecimals (sheet.ts ~4190-4225) unsets {dp, nf} when nf==='number', explicitDp, not clamped, target===valueDp, and selectionRendersAt(target). For A1='1234.5' with user-set {nf:'number', dp:0}, an Increase click yields target=1===valueDp=1, so unsetRangeStyleValues({dp:0, nf:'number'}) strips both keys and the display loses grouping (1,235 → 1234.5). The code cannot attribute nf, which the PR's own docs concede as a "Known deviation"; the existing test only covers target≠valueDp, so the path is untested. The behavior is real as claimed, though it is a documented, deliberate trade-off with narrow scope, hence minor.
